system_prompt:
You are an eighth-grade student taking the TIMSS mathematics test for students in your grade. Do your best on each question, as you would on a real test, using the mathematics you have learned in school so far.

The pictures, figures, and graphs of the test booklet are described in words, and its tables are written out. When a question asks you to draw, mark, shade, label, or fill in something on a figure, graph, or table, describe exactly what you would draw or write, and where. When a question asks you to show your work or explain your answer, include the work or explanation in your answer. For a multiple-choice question, choose one option.
user_prompt:
480 students were asked to name their favorite sport. The results are shown in this table.

| Sport | Number of Students |
| :--- | :--- |
| Hockey | 60 |
| Football | 180 |
| Tennis | 120 |
| Basketball | 120 |

Use the information in the table to complete and label this pie chart.

[Image: A circle with a point in the middle, and 8 equally spaced points on the circumference of the circle. The circle is labeled “Popularity of Sports.”]

Figure, described in words:
A circle labeled "Popularity of Sports" at the top. The circle contains a dot at its center and 8 equally spaced dots along its circumference, located at 12 o'clock, 1:30, 3 o'clock, 4:30, 6 o'clock, 7:30, 9 o'clock, and 10:30.

answer.description: Your answer to the question, as you would write it in the test booklet, with any work, explanation, or description of a drawing that the question asks for.
answer.title: Answer

output.answer: Work: Total = 480 students. Hockey 60/480 = 12.5% = 45 degrees (one 45-degree sector). Football 180/480 = 37.5% = 135 degrees (three 45-degree sectors). Tennis 120/480 = 25% = 90 degrees (two sectors). Basketball 120/480 = 25% = 90 degrees (two sectors). Check: 1 + 3 + 2 + 2 = 8 sectors, which matches the 8 equally spaced points. Drawing: Draw a straight line (radius) from the center to each of the 8 points on the circumference. Starting at the 12 o'clock point and going clockwise, mark the sectors as follows. Hockey is the sector from 12 o'clock to the 1:30 point (45 degrees). Football is the sector from the 1:30 point to the 6 o'clock point (135 degrees). Tennis is the sector from the 6 o'clock point to the 9 o'clock point (90 degrees). Basketball is the sector from the 9 o'clock point to the 12 o'clock point (90 degrees). Label each sector with its sport name and its share, for example 'Hockey 12.5% (60)', 'Football 37.5% (180)', 'Tennis 25% (120)', 'Basketball 25% (120)', placed inside or next to its sector. Give the chart the title 'Popularity of Sports' (already there) and add a key or the labels so each sector is clearly identified.
